name: add_annotation
description: Attach a human-style ground-truth label (pass/fail + optional critique) to a trace or session, optionally as a golden label and optionally tied to a failure mode/cluster. Writes to the ground_truth_labels store; re-labeling the same target supersedes the prior label. Use to record verdicts an agent has judged.

name: add_rejected_fix_to_dataset
description: Add a REJECTED fix (a PR closed without merging or with changes requested — review_id from get_fix_pr_reviews) to a dataset as 'known bad fix' cases: the inputs the fix was verified on plus the traces the rejected fix produced, tagged with the reviewer's reason, so future evals catch what the reviewer caught. Defaults to the fix's own regression dataset (dataset_id overrides). Idempotent. Fails with a clear message when the PR was not rejected or the fix has no recorded verification cases. Snapshot a new golden version for runs to see it.

dataset_id.description: Target dataset id (default: the fix's own).

name: add_to_dataset
description: Add traces/sessions to an existing dataset (by id or name). Returns how many were added vs skipped (duplicates). Use to grow a curated dataset over time. Each new item gets a DRAFT of its expected tool calls copied from the trace (unreviewed, never graded): correct it with set_expected_tool_calls.

name: attach_verification_run
description: Record an EXISTING pre-prod run as a fix's proof — for a run you created yourself (create_preprod_run, or `neens eval run --create` in CI against an agent Neens cannot call) rather than with run_verification, which creates and attaches its own. The run must be in this agent and replay the remediation's proof golden dataset (the one get_fix_bundle's `proof` names), else the call is refused with the dataset it needs; a run still awaiting traces or scoring may be attached, a failed/cancelled one may not. Replaces any earlier proof run. The reply carries proofBound plus `warnings` when the run is not scored by the proof judge or froze an older golden version. Poll get_verification_run for its verdict.

run_id.description: Pre-prod run id to attach (required; from create_preprod_run or list_preprod_runs).

name: cancel_ambient_run
description: Cancel a queued, running or waiting Scout run. It stops before its next step (a waiting run stops waiting) and is marked cancelled; a finished run cannot be cancelled.

name: cancel_preprod_run
description: Cancel a pre-prod run that is still awaiting traces or running. Terminal (a run that already completed/failed/cancelled) is refused rather than rewritten — cancelling is not a way to discard a result.

name: check_judge_agreement
description: Check an llm_prompt judge against reviewers' pass/fail verdicts WITHOUT deploying it: scores the judge on up to `limit` traces a person already labelled (newest first; optionally only members of dataset_id) and returns how many it agreed with, its false alarms (judge failed, reviewer passed) and misses (judge passed, reviewer failed), Cohen's kappa, and the disagreements. Stores nothing. Spends one model call per trace on the agent's LLM connection.

version_id.description: Judge version; omit for the current version.

dataset_id.description: Only traces in this dataset (id or name).

name: compare_preprod_runs
description: Line up TWO OR MORE pre-prod runs against each other over the same frozen golden version: per-run pass rate, average score and cost/latency/step traits, plus a matrix keyed by golden prompt with one cell per run. Name one run as baseline_run_id and each row also reports which runs REGRESSED against it, and `regressionAnalysis` maps each other run to its severity-graded, grouped regressions against that baseline (as in get_preprod_comparison). Every run must snapshot the same dataset version (list_preprod_runs shows it) — otherwise the request is refused rather than aligned on mismatched prompts.

run_ids.description: Two or more pre-prod run ids sharing one dataset version (required, max 25).

baseline_run_id.description: One of run_ids, to mark per-row regressions.

name: create_code_enrichment
description: Create a CODE (custom_python) enrichment: Python that tags each trace with typed values (e.g. quotes_refund: boolean, refund_amount: number) that you can filter, chart and build datasets on. Test the code with test_code_enrichment BEFORE creating. The code is a top-level `def enrich(target)` or `def enrich(target, ctx)`; `target` is a dict of the required_data keys (input, output, messages, context, metadata). It returns a dict keyed by the output field keys, each value of that field's type (boolean → true/false, number, string, enum → one of its values, array → a list of scalars); a key that is not a declared field or a value of the wrong type fails the trace, and a field left out is simply not set. `ctx.skip("reason")` skips a trace. It runs in the same isolated sandbox as code judges: NO network, nothing installable, no secrets, nothing persists between traces. Needs a plan with code enrichments (Gold). Saved as a draft that does not run until deploy_enrichment.

output_fields.description: The values the code returns, e.g. [{"key": "quotes_refund", "type": "boolean"}, {"key": "refund_amount", "type": "number"}]. type is boolean | number | string | enum (with values) | array.

runtime.description: custom_python: runtime id to pin (default: the current one).

requirements.description: custom_python: requirements.txt lines the runtime must already meet (nothing is installed), e.g. "numpy>=2".

capabilities.description: custom_python: {"llm": true} to allow ctx.llm calls through the agent's LLM connection. Off by default.

environment_id.description: Optional: a code environment id (list_code_environments) whose extra packages the code imports.

required_data.description: Data to feed the code (input/output/messages/context/metadata; default input/output/messages/metadata).

name: create_dataset
description: Create a dataset in the current project. If session_ids/trace_ids are given, the dataset is created AND populated from that selection (optionally as an immutable golden v1 via `golden`); otherwise an empty manual dataset is created. Datasets are a Silver+ tier feature. Use to curate failing traces for evaluation.

name: create_enrichment_version
description: Save a new version of a code (custom_python) enrichment — changed code, limits, runtime, requirements, capabilities, environment or required_data; everything you do not pass carries over from the current version (limits merge key by key). The new version becomes current at once: an enabled enrichment runs it from its next run. Test the change with test_code_enrichment first.

runtime.description: custom_python: runtime id to pin (default: the current one).

requirements.description: custom_python: requirements.txt lines the runtime must already meet (nothing is installed), e.g. "numpy>=2".

capabilities.description: custom_python: {"llm": true} to allow ctx.llm calls through the agent's LLM connection. Off by default.

environment_id.description: Optional: a code environment id (list_code_environments) whose extra packages the code imports.

required_data.description: Data to feed the code (input/output/messages/context/metadata; default input/output/messages/metadata).

name: create_golden_version
description: Snapshot a dataset's CURRENT items into a new immutable version and mark it golden (pass golden:false for a plain snapshot). One golden version per dataset — goldening a new one un-goldens the previous. This is the step between curating a dataset and running a pre-prod eval or a model sweep against it, both of which replay a frozen version so results stay comparable.

golden.description: Mark it the dataset's golden version (default true).

name: create_judge
description: Create a judge (scorer) in the project. Default type llm_prompt: provide a prompt_template (use {target} for the trace/session), optional criteria, and required_data (input/output/messages/context/expected_output/metadata). Or type custom_python, a CODE judge, for a check that is a rule (a pattern, a schema, a word budget): provide code, and test it with test_code_judge BEFORE creating. The code is a top-level `def judge(target)` or `def judge(target, ctx)`; `target` is a dict of the required_data keys (output, input, messages, context, expected_output, metadata). It returns {"score": float} on the default 0–1 scale, or {"label": …} when output_spec is binary/categorical (the shape MUST match output_spec, or every trace fails with an invalid return value); `ctx.skip("reason")` skips a trace. The code runs in an isolated sandbox with NO network: external APIs, URLs and downloads all fail (requests imports but every call fails), nothing can be installed (only the runtime's packages), there are no secrets, and nothing persists between traces. The one way out is ctx.llm, with capabilities {"llm": true}. Needs a plan with code judges (Gold). list_code_runtimes lists the packages; list_code_environments lists custom environments with more (pass environment_id). Or type composite, to combine existing judges (list_judges) into one score: provide components, and test it with test_code_judge type=composite. A composite combines judges that already exist in this project into one 0–1 score; each component's score arrives normalized to 0–1 (a binary judge's pass = 1.0, fail = 0.0). method weighted_sum (default) averages the components by weight; method expression computes a formula over component metric keys (the judge name lowercased, non-letters → _; min, max, abs, round and + - * / allowed), e.g. "min(cites_sources, polite_tone)" with threshold 1.0 passes only when BOTH pass; method custom_python runs code `def combine(components, ctx)` (components = {metric_key: 0–1 or None}) returning {"score": float}. A composite has no output_spec, prompt_template or criteria. Or type pairwise, a BLIND A/B preference judge: provide criteria only; it is run with start_pairwise_comparison, never deployed, and is advisory. Creates the judge + version 1 (experimental). Follow with deploy_judge then run_eval to score traces.

type.description: Default 'llm_prompt'. 'custom_python' = a code judge; 'composite' = combines existing judges; 'pairwise' = compares two answers blind (criteria only).

level.description: Default 'project' (this agent). 'org' / 'platform' apply it more widely and need a company admin for code judges.

required_data.description: Data to feed the judge (default input/output/messages/metadata).

require_evidence.description: llm_prompt: require every verdict to cite a verbatim quote of the trace (default true for a new judge); a verdict whose quotes are not in the trace is skipped as ungrounded_verdict.

code.description: custom_python only: the Python source (required for that type).

output_spec.description: The judge's scale. Omit for 0–1. {"type": "binary", "pass_label": "pass", "fail_label": "fail"} for pass/fail; {"type": "categorical", "labels": [worst … best]}; {"type": "numeric_range", "min": 1, "max": 10}.

runtime.description: custom_python: runtime id to pin (default: the current one).

requirements.description: custom_python: requirements.txt lines the runtime must already meet (nothing is installed), e.g. "numpy>=2".

capabilities.description: custom_python: {"llm": true} to allow ctx.llm calls through the agent's LLM connection. Off by default.

environment_id.description: custom_python: id of a ready custom code environment (list_code_environments) whose extra packages the code imports. It must belong to this agent or be shared across the company; the judge is pinned to its exact build.

components.description: composite only (required): the judges to combine, by id (list_judges) or exact name, each with an optional weight (default: equal).

expression.description: composite method=expression: the formula over component metric keys, e.g. "min(cites_sources, polite_tone)".

threshold.description: composite: the 0–1 score at or above which it passes (default 0.7).

min_components.description: composite: skip a trace with fewer scored components than this (default 1).

missing_policy.description: composite: a trace missing a component score is skipped (default) or failed.

both_orders.description: pairwise: judge every pair in both A/B orders (default true); a verdict that flips with the order counts as a tie.

include_reference.description: pairwise: show the golden reference answer to the judge when the item has one (default true).

name: create_judge_version
description: Add a new VERSION to an existing judge instead of creating a copy. Pass the judge id and what changes: for an llm_prompt judge prompt_template, criteria, output_spec and/or required_data; for a custom_python (code) judge code, output_spec, limits, requirements, capabilities, runtime, environment_id and/or required_data (test new code with test_code_judge first). Every other setting carries over from the latest version. The new version becomes the judge's current version but existing deployments keep scoring with their version: follow with deploy_judge (the reply's versionId), run_eval, then disable_deployment on the old deployment. A project API key can only version judges that belong to its own project.

prompt_template.description: llm_prompt: new evaluation prompt; {target} is interpolated.

require_evidence.description: llm_prompt: true opts the judge into evidence-quoted verdicts (an ungrounded verdict is skipped, not scored); false turns it off. Omit to keep the current setting.

code.description: custom_python only: the Python source (required for that type).

output_spec.description: The judge's scale. Omit for 0–1. {"type": "binary", "pass_label": "pass", "fail_label": "fail"} for pass/fail; {"type": "categorical", "labels": [worst … best]}; {"type": "numeric_range", "min": 1, "max": 10}.

runtime.description: custom_python: runtime id to pin (default: the current one).

requirements.description: custom_python: requirements.txt lines the runtime must already meet (nothing is installed), e.g. "numpy>=2".

capabilities.description: custom_python: {"llm": true} to allow ctx.llm calls through the agent's LLM connection. Off by default.

environment_id.description: custom_python: id of a ready custom code environment (list_code_environments) whose extra packages the code imports. It must belong to this agent or be shared across the company; the judge is pinned to its exact build.

note.description: What changed and why, shown in the version history.

name: create_preprod_run
description: Create a pre-prod evaluation run over a dataset's frozen golden version at a candidate `version_label` (the branch/commit/deploy under test). It is created in `awaiting_traces` and runs NOTHING until start_preprod_run. runner_mode 'push' means Neens calls your endpoint itself and REQUIRES agent_connection_id; 'runner' (the default) means Neens waits for your own harness's traces. Gate it with min_pass_rate / max_regressions. Use run_verification instead when you are proving one specific remediation's fix.

dataset_id.description: Dataset id or name whose golden version is replayed (required).

dataset_version_id.description: Explicit frozen version instead of golden.

agent_connection_id.description: Registered agent_http connection; REQUIRED for runner_mode 'push'.

judge_deployment_ids.description: Graders (default: the project's scoreable deployed judges).

replay_mode.description: How multi-turn items are replayed: 'scripted' (the default) sends the recorded user turns in order on one conversation.

scoring_grain.description: 'conversation' (default) grades the whole transcript; 'turn' also grades every reply and fails the item on any failing turn.

baseline_kind.description: What to compare against (default: 7d prod window). 'branch' = the newest completed run on baseline_branch for the same golden version.

baseline_run_id.description: The prior run, for baseline_kind preprod_run.

baseline_branch.description: The branch, for baseline_kind branch (e.g. main).

baseline_range.description: Window for a prod_window baseline, e.g. 7d.

block_on.description: Gate: fail on a statistically SIGNIFICANT regression of this severity or worse (a noisy drop on a small set does not block).

max_regressions_per_failure_mode.description: Gate: max regressions allowed in any ONE failure mode.

max_error_rate.description: Gate: share of items (0-1) allowed to error or not run before the run fails on coverage (default 0.1).

name: create_standing_instruction
description: Give Scout a standing instruction on this agent, for yourself: text says what to do in your own words ("Every Monday, review this agent and tell me what changed"). Give EITHER cron + timezone (five cron fields, e.g. '0 9 * * 1' = Mondays 09:00; at most about once an hour) OR condition_kind (an event Scout reacts to: insight_opened, alert_fired, clustering_finished, efficacy_verdict, judge_alignment_drop, agent_version_seen, autonomy_suspended, action_reopened) with optional condition_target_id. slack=true also DMs results to you in Slack. once=true ends it after the first result. Results go only to you. There is a limit per person; over it this is refused and nothing is replaced (pausing does not free a place; ending does). Undo with end_standing_instruction. No agent tool can delete an instruction: only the person can, in Settings.

text.description: What Scout should do, in your words.

name.description: A short label (default: the first line).

condition_kind.description: Fire on this event instead of a schedule.

condition_target_id.description: Only events about this judge, fix, next action or agent version.

slack.description: Also DM results to you in Slack.

name: deploy_enrichment
description: Turn a code (custom_python) enrichment on. trigger 'on_ingest' enriches newly ingested traces automatically (capped per day); 'manual' (default) enables it for runs started from the Neens app. sample_rate (0 < r <= 1, e.g. 0.1 = 10%) makes on_ingest enrich only that fraction of new traces, the same traces on every redelivery; omitted keeps the current rate (1 = all). Existing traces are not back-filled by this call.

sample_rate.description: Fraction of newly ingested traces on_ingest enriches (0.1 = 10%). Omit to keep the current rate.

name: deploy_judge
description: Deploy (enable) a judge version so it can run. Only the judge id is required: OMIT version_id to deploy the judge's LATEST version, or pass either a version id (list_judges → versions[].id / latestVersionId, or create_judge's latestVersionId) or a version NUMBER like "2". Never guess a version id — if it cannot be resolved the tool answers with the judge's real version ids. Re-deploying a version already enabled with the same trigger AND pass cutoff returns the existing deployment instead of a duplicate; changing either is a real, separate deployment. trigger_policy 'manual' scores on demand; 'on_new_trace' scores every new trace. The reply carries resolvedVersionId and the deployment id run_eval needs.

version_id.description: OPTIONAL. A judge version id, or a version number like "2". Omit to deploy the latest version.

name: disable_deployment
description: Disable a judge deployment so it stops scoring — e.g. a superseded version after deploy_judge put the new one live, or a judge that is misbehaving. Non-destructive: the deployment, its scores and run history are kept, and deploy_judge can enable the version again. Pass the deployment id from list_judges (judges[].deployments[].id).

judge_id.description: Optional: the deployment's judge id (looked up when omitted).

name: end_standing_instruction
description: Stop one of your standing instructions for good: it never runs again and frees its place under your limit; past results stay readable. There is no undo — create a new one instead. This is the furthest an agent can go: no agent tool can DELETE an instruction. If the person asks to delete one, end it and tell them deleting is done by them in Settings → This agent → Scout.

name: export_dataset
description: Export a dataset — returned as a MANIFEST, never as the file: exact row count, row schema, a sha256 checksum of the full body, its byte size, and a 3-row head sample, plus the URL to GET the whole export (json or csv) over plain HTTP with the same credential. `complete:false` means the sample is a head, not the data. Inlining a real export would exceed the tool-result cap and come back silently truncated but still parseable, so it is never inlined.

name: export_dataset_version
description: Export one immutable dataset VERSION as a manifest — same contract as export_dataset (row count, schema, sha256 checksum, head sample, retrieval URL; never the inlined body), plus which version it is and whether it is golden. Use to hand a frozen evaluation set to another system by reference.

name: generate_remediation
description: Generate a grounded remediation (suggested fix) for a failure cluster or failure mode. Provide cluster_id or failure_mode_id. The generator classifies the failure locus from real evidence (error strings, HTTP status, span kind/status), so it may return an agent-fixable fix (prompt/tool change), an ADVISORY for a downstream/upstream service failure (naming the owning service, not a prompt edit), a working_as_intended note when a guardrail fired correctly, or a needs_grounding item held out of the actionable backlog until it is concrete and confident. Degrades deterministically when no LLM connection is configured. Use to propose a fix for a diagnosed failure.

name: get_ablation_run
description: One ablation run: per removed section its verdict (earns_its_place | no_measurable_effect | removing_it_helps | pending | failed | no_data), quality delta with interval, the noise band, cost delta (null = unpriced) and latency delta, against the full prompt.

name: get_action_inbox
description: Start here when asked what to fix next, what changed or how things are going. One call returns the Insights action inbox: lead (the page's three plain sentences: failure trend vs the previous window, the spend that went to failing runs or that spend isn't priced yet, and the top action with its recorded owner or none; quote them rather than recomputing), what changed versus the previous window (new failures, regressions, anomalies, fixes not yet applied, fixes that held), how many open items sit at each fix-loop stage (needs_fix, fix_proposed, in_pr, verified, downstream), and the ranked queue of issues (at most 20) with severity, sessions affected now vs before, growth, estimated wasted spend and where each fix stands. Each row carries the ids the next step needs: targetId (pass to get_failure_mode when targetType is cluster), fixSource (cluster_id / failure_mode_id for generate_remediation when stage is needs_fix) and remediationId (for get_remediation / update_remediation). Unlike list_failure_modes (the latest clustering run, unranked by impact) and list_open_remediations (fixes only), this ranks failures AND their fix status together. A null count means it could not be read, never zero. Scoped to this connection's project; a connection spanning several agents gets a failure with the same name on 2+ agents as ONE row with agentCount and children (act on each child's ids).

range.description: Time window compared with the previous window of the same length (default 7d).

stage.description: Only rows at this step of the fix loop: needs_fix (no fix yet), fix_proposed (a fix awaits review), in_pr (a PR is open), verified (the fix held), downstream (a service outside the agent owns it).

name: get_ambient_run
description: One Scout run in full: what triggered it (with the ids of the events folded into it), the tools each turn called, and the finding — title, summary, confidence and the ids it cites — plus any plan it recommends for a person to approve. The finding is agent-written (author=agent), carries only links checked against what the run read, says whether it was translated (translation.status: source, translated or untranslated + reason), and recurrenceOf names the earlier run whose conclusion this one re-checked. wait is the job it is (or last was) waiting on: kind, id, status (waiting, resumed, expired, cancelled), the job's status and the deadline.

name: get_ambient_settings
description: This agent's Scout settings and guardrails: its level (off, suggest, investigate, act), the write tools it may run itself at act (actTools; empty by default) and every tool that can be allowed (actEligible), the investigation budget for the period with what is spent and reserved so far, the caps on runs per day and concurrent runs, the per-run ceilings, whether it is paused (the kill switch), the LLM connection investigations use, and any targets held after repeated failed runs (with their ids, for release_ambient_quarantine).

name: get_ambient_signal_quality
description: How useful people found each kind of next action on this agent over the last 30 days: per kind the useful and not-useful ratings, the useful rate (null when unrated), and whether the ranking demotes the kind or mutes it from the list. A kind moves only after enough ratings (minRatings). Ratings by AI agents and API keys are not counted.

name: get_ambient_trace_project
description: Whether Scout's own traces go to this workspace's built-in agent project, and which project that is (projectId, set only when you can open it). With run_id, also the trace that Scout run sent there (sessionId + projectId): open it with get_trace under that project to see each model call and tool call the run made. A run whose trace was not sent (the project was off) or that you cannot open is not found.

run_id.description: Optional: a Scout run's id, to get its trace.

name: get_business_kpis
description: List the project's Business KPIs (a measure promoted to a committed target) with current value, whether the target is met, and the trend. Pass kpi_id to drill into one KPI, including the failure clusters eroding it. A null value reads targetStatus 'unknown' (never 'missed'). A KPI with targetWindowDays is judged at that window whatever range you ask for; targetJudgedAt then names the window and its value, so say the verdict was judged at that window. trend compares the last 7 complete days with the 7 before, pooled, and carries both readings and both sample sizes; a null trend is UNKNOWN, not flat — say why from trendUnavailable (thin_sample means a week was too small; trendSamples has the counts). The list also returns lead — the page's one-sentence summary (money recovered or lost per month, and the KPI still off target); quote lead.sentences rather than recomputing — and drafts, KPIs configured but not yet committed. lead.recovered counts only fixes measured against a holdout (causal); lead.correlational is KPI movement beside fixes with no holdout: report it separately as not proven, never add the two. Use for 'how are our KPIs doing', 'are we hitting our targets', 'what target should we set', or 'what's dragging KPI X down'. lead.action 'set_targets' means lead.gaps.noTarget KPIs have a value but no target, so they read unknown; pass propose_targets=true to also get targetProposals — a target proposed per such KPI from its last 28 complete days. status 'proposed' carries proposedTarget (the baseline rounded to hold the current level); 'insufficient_history', 'no_value' and 'baseline_at_limit' carry none — say so, never invent one. A proposal is a suggestion: an admin confirms or edits it with Set targets on the Business KPIs page.

kpi_id.description: Drill into one KPI by id (from a prior list). Omit to list all.

range.description: Time window token, e.g. 7d / 30d (default the server default).

propose_targets.description: List mode only: also return a proposed target for each active KPI that has none (read-only; nothing is saved).

name: get_cluster_exemplars
description: The most REPRESENTATIVE traces of a cluster — the members nearest its centroid, with their distance. A short read to understand what a failure mode looks like before pulling the whole set with list_traces(cluster_id=…).

name: get_component
description: Get one component (kind + name, from list_components): its measures, its most recent invocations (trace id, version, who invoked it, status, duration, error) and how many papercuts the agent filed about it. A component not invoked in the window is a not-found.

name: get_cost_quality_brief
description: Read the one-line Cost & Quality brief for a page of this agent: what its cost and quality numbers say and the one next step. page is overview (spend split, unpriced models, a proven saving), agent (has this version's model been measured by a sweep, and is a cheaper model proven), judge (do the judges have enough human labels, does one disagree with them, is a judge model unpriced) or sweep (the verdict of one model sweep; needs sweep_id). Returns rule = {reasonCode, params, action} — params are the figures the page shows (USD, null = unpriced, never $0; percentages 0-100) — and scoutText when Scout has already worded it for these exact numbers (null otherwise; this tool never asks Scout to write). version defaults to the live version; use list_agent_versions for the labels. For page=overview it also returns overview: savings (state available / none_proven / partly_measured / not_measured / nothing_to_measure, monthlyUsd, and how many versions' agent models were tested and judges have enough labels), nextActions (the Do next list: one entry per cause — proven_saving, agent_untested, sweep_below_bar, judge_below_bar, judges_need_labels, model_unpriced, sweep_unpriced, sweep_void, sweep_unranked, sweep_no_quality, judge_single_model — ranked by what unlocks a saving, with count, the subjects and the action), and where the money goes per version (traces, agent and judge spend, per1kUsd per 1,000 traces, models, model evidence) and per model, with test and replay labels folded into one row, and pricing: partial + unpricedModels, the prompt-cache reads and writes inside the agent's input tokens (cacheReadInputTokens, cacheWriteInputTokens; spend is cache-aware, they bill at their own rates) and cacheEstimated = some cache tokens billed at the input rate because the model has no cache rate (cacheInputRateModels names them; the spend is then an estimate). page=overview also returns costPerOutcome: what one GOOD outcome (a resolved case or a successful task, as the project declared it; outcome names which, choices the declared ones, pass outcome to pick) cost in agent spend — usd over decidedCases with goodOutcomes, matchRatePct = share of cases with an outcome (lowCoverage under 50) — or usd null with a reason (no_outcome_declared, thin_sample, no_good_outcomes, no_spend_data, unpriced, no_cases, outcome_unavailable); each byVersion row carries perOutcomeUsd beside agentPerTraceUsd. page=judge also returns minLabels and judges = one row per judge: agreementPct with your human labels over ALL labels (ignores version and window; null below minLabels labelled traces — see labelled), flagRatePct and costPer1kUsd for the selected version + window, and nextStep = {step: label|fix_judge|keep|switch, reasonCode, params}. For page=agent it also returns agentModel: the model decision for that version (state switch/hold/untested/no_quality, reasonCode, confidence proven/likely, the sweep it rests on, the version's finished sweeps) and carriedForward — when the version has no sweep, the newest finished sweep measured on ANOTHER version of this agent, with that version, its age in days and its result code. Evidence from another version is not a verdict for this one: re-run it on this version.

page.description: Which Cost & Quality page the brief is for (required).

outcome.description: page=overview: which declared good outcome costPerOutcome is about (default: the committed one).

window.description: Trailing window in days, e.g. '7d' (default) or '30d'.

name: get_current_project
description: Report which project THIS connection is scoped to — its name, id, org and company — plus how the scope was set (credentialKind, scopePinned) and your role. A project API key and an SSO/OAuth MCP token each pin one project, so this is the answer to 'which project am I connected to?'. Call it FIRST in a session to confirm the project (e.g. after an SSO sign-in) before reading or writing. Returns projectId=null with a note when no single project is pinned (a user session picks its active project per request).

name: get_dataset_items
description: Read a dataset's LIVE items (input, expected output, captured output, source trace). Optional text search `q` and `kind` filter. `total` is how many items the dataset has and `returned` how many came back — `complete: false` means you are looking at a page, not the set.

name: get_dataset_stats
description: Read one dataset's health (the dataset page's summary): datasetType (static, snapshot = a filter dataset that grows only on Sync now, streaming = auto-synced hourly, cluster), item totals and items added in the last 7 days, expected-output coverage, expected tool calls reviewed vs draft (a draft is never graded), the session/trace/json mix, freshness (last edit, last + next sync, pendingMatches = matching sessions a sync would add), a growth timeline (axis added = when items joined, trace = when their source traces started; the creation backfill is reported separately; idleSince flags a streaming dataset that stopped growing), saved versions (which is golden), what replays it (eval gates, failure-mode regression sets, recent pre-prod runs with the version they pinned) and data-quality counts (items with no captured output, duplicate inputs, items whose source trace is gone). null means unknown or not applicable, never zero.

name: get_dataset_version_items
description: Read one immutable version's frozen snapshot items. Same shape as get_dataset_items but for a version, so it never changes under a run. `version` is the integer version NUMBER from list_dataset_versions, not the version id.

name: get_eval_run
description: Open one evaluation run by id: status, per-status task counts, the judge's verdict counts, and a page of its scored TASKS (target id, score, label, reason, error). `passed`/`failed` are verdicts over the `scored` targets and passRate = passed/scored (null when nothing was scored) — report THIS as the pass rate. `errored` counts targets that could not be scored. completionRate is the share of attempted targets that finished scoring, NOT a pass rate; successRate is a deprecated alias of completionRate. `taskTotal` is the run's whole size; `tasks` is at most `limit` rows from `offset`. Use after run_eval to see what a judge actually decided, per trace. A task's `evidence` is the verbatim trace text its verdict cited; `skipReason: ungrounded_verdict` means the judge's quotes were not in the trace, so no score was recorded.

name: get_failure_mode
description: Fetch one failure cluster/mode by id: label, description, root cause, remediation summary, up to 10 member session ids plus memberTotal (how many traces the mode holds — list_traces with cluster_id pages them all), and its distribution across agent versions (members per version vs that version's traffic, so a failure only one build produces stands out). Use after list_failure_modes to drill into a specific mode. fixabilityVerdict says whether a patch can fix the failure: `patchable` (a fix run verified a patch), `capability_limited` (a model sweep on the failure's golden set shows the current model below the bar while a stronger model clears it — recommend a model change via that sweep, do not start another fix run; Neens never switches models itself) or `unknown` (follow recommendation.action, e.g. run_model_sweep on recommendation.datasetId). `paths` groups the mode's recent sessions by how they fail (kind: retryLoop | retryOnce | recoveredRetry | recovered | stopsAtFailure | continuesAfter | noErrorStep | other), each with its count, the step it first fails at (and causeStep when that step received a tool's error), the retried step's run range, the most common error and example session ids for get_trace. componentOwner names the skill / MCP server / sub-agent / tool the mode's failures start inside (owner with share and sessions; null with a reason when the evidence is thin, split or unattributed) — target a fix there.

name: get_fix_bundle
description: Fetch a remediation's FIX BUNDLE. For an ACTIONABLE fix this is the paste-ready markdown brief (root cause + typed before/after fix spec + redacted failing exemplars), `verification` — the exact run_verification arguments that prove the fix — the gate policy, the proof evals, and the acceptance criteria: everything a coding agent needs to implement and prove the fix. `evalCommand` is an optional CI one-liner for the `neens` CLI, which is not yet published. The reply also carries failureLocus / actionability / owningComponent: when actionability is `advisory` the bundle is NOT a prompt fix — it describes a downstream/upstream service failure, names the owning service, and recommends a resilience/ownership action rather than an agent edit. `proofAlignment` says which judge + golden dataset prove the fix and whether that judge is human-anchored (Cohen's κ, nGold): an unanchored judge's pass rate is not proof. Requires remediation_id (from list_open_remediations).

name: get_fix_pr_reviews
description: Read how human reviewers received this agent's fix pull requests: per PR its state (open|merged|closed_unmerged), the review decision (approved|changes_requested|commented|none), approvals, change requests, follow-up commits (iterations), the reviewers' rejection reason and a short timeline (comment text is PII-redacted). negativeLabel is 'rejected' (closed without merging) or 'changes_requested'. Also returns acceptance: the fix PR acceptance rate with n (null when n is 0 — unknown, not 0%). Filter with remediation_id or fix_run_id. Read it BEFORE implementing a fix: a rejected earlier fix's reason must be addressed by the next one.

name: get_fix_run
description: Poll a fix run by id for its status (queued|applying|verifying|pr_opened|failed|drafted|cancelled), attempt count, pass^k eval report, verifying judges, the opened PR url, and the failure report if it could not be verified. Use to check a run started by start_fix_run.

name: get_judge_alignment
description: How well each judge agrees with HUMAN gold labels, as Neens measured it: precision, recall, TNR and Cohen's kappa (a judge FAIL is the positive class), the number of gold-labeled traces compared (nGold) and when it was measured. Pass judge_id (an id from list_judges, or the judge's name) for one judge — the reply then also carries the LIVE count of false alarms and misses. Use this instead of computing agreement yourself, e.g. after add_annotation + run_eval.

judge_id.description: Judge id (or name). Omit for every judge.

name: get_judge_runs
description: List the eval runs of ONE judge, newest first: status, targets scored, average score and pass rate per run, plus an active/historic summary. Per run, `passed` and `failed` are the judge's verdicts over `scored` targets, `errored` counts targets that could not be scored, and passRate = passed/scored (null when nothing was scored). `ungrounded` counts verdicts discarded because the judge cited no evidence quote found in the trace (recorded as skips, never as pass or fail). Use to find the run id to open with get_eval_run, or to see whether a judge has ever scored.

name: get_model_sweep
description: Poll a model sweep by id: its status (queued|awaiting_traces|running|completed|completed_with_failures|failed|cancelled|void), the pinned conditions, the cost estimate, and a PER-ARM summary — model, status, pass^k as greens/k, and terminal vs total runs. Partial results are normal: read the per-arm status rather than waiting for the whole sweep. Two honesty rules to respect when reporting: a status of `void` means the arms did NOT run under identical conditions, so the arms are NOT comparable and voidReason says why — never rank them; and an estimate with partial=true excludes the unpriced models it names, so its totalUsd is a floor, not the cost.

name: get_model_sweep_comparison
description: DECIDE a model sweep: the N-way comparison of its arms and the answer — which model to ship. Returns one verdict sentence plus a per-arm leaderboard (pass rate WITH its sample size n and a 95% confidence interval, pass^k greens/k, p95 latency, cost per case, token-limit truncation rate over LLM calls that reported a finish reason, regressions vs the declared baseline arm) and a verdict PER AGENT, because the answer legitimately differs by agent. Four rules to respect when reporting the result: (1) comparable=false means the sweep is VOID — its arms did not run under identical conditions, so never rank them, whatever their numbers say; (2) costPerCaseUsd=null means UNPRICED, never free — such an arm cannot win 'cheapest' and appears in verdict.excluded with reasonCode 'unpriced' ('partially_priced' when only some cases had a price — its figure is a floor); cost.noUsageCases / cost.unknownModelCases say why cases are unpriced when no model rate is missing (traces without token counts or a model name); latency avgMs/p95Ms=null means no measured duration, not 0 ms; (3) rate=null means no data, not 0%; (4) an item counts as passed only when it passed EVERY repeat run — 2 of 3 is not a pass, and flakyItems counts the difference. decision.settle says what would settle a 'likely' answer: more_items gives addItems NEW golden-set items (each runs passK times per model) and holds only if the observed rate holds; not_settleable_by_items means no practical set would. sweepWarnings code 'provider_errors' names an arm whose cases largely failed at the model provider (HTTP 429 rate limits / 5xx): its pass rate and cost measure the provider, not the model — say so, and suggest re-running the sweep at a lower request rate or with more retries (decision.settle 'rerun_provider_errors'; cost.providerErrorCases are no-usage cases that need no price). Read-only: computes nothing new and spends nothing.

bar.description: Pass-rate bar in 0-1 to decide against. Default: the sweep's pinned gate min_pass_rate, else the deployment's success threshold. The response's bar.source says which was used.

baseline_arm.description: Arm id to compare against. Default: the DECLARED incumbent (position 0) — never the best performer, since a baseline picked after seeing the results is not a baseline.

name: get_next_actions
description: What to do next on this agent: the ranked next best actions the person would see on the agent's card (a primary action and up to four more), already filtered to what this connection may see. Each action has id, kind, title, why (impact), target (targetType + targetId: a cluster is a failure mode for get_failure_mode), state, canRun (false means the caller lacks a capability in requires, or is an API key), and steps (the tools a run would call, or a link when it is done outside Neens). Pass action_id for one action in any state, including who ran, handed off or closed it. Org and company actions (scopeKind org or company) span agents: their parts list only the agents this connection can see, and their counts come from those parts. An action is rules-written; its finding (when present) is Scout's own investigation of it — agent-written, with its runId for get_ambient_run. A retest_live_version action (test on release) has release: the new live version, the sweep it repeats, what is missing, and autoRun (what autonomy will do, e.g. ready, autonomy_off, no_budget, over_budget, unpriced); running it only starts that sweep. Use it for "what should I do next?"; use get_action_inbox for what changed and the fix-loop queue.

action_id.description: One action's id (from a previous call). Omit for the list.

scope.description: all (default), agent (this agent only), or rollups (org and company actions only).

name: get_pairwise_comparison
description: Read a blind pairwise comparison by comparison_id (with a page of per-item raw verdicts in each order), or list the comparisons on a sweep_id / run_id. The result gives each side's win rate over DECISIVE pairs with a 95% Wilson interval, ties reported separately (orderInconsistentTies = verdicts that flipped with the order), and a state: insufficient_evidence (fewer than minDecisive decisive pairs), no_clear_preference (the interval includes 50%), or x_preferred / y_preferred. Never report a winner when state says otherwise, and never report a rate=null as 0%. humanAgreement compares the judge with blind human preference labels (Cohen's kappa; null when the labels cannot support one). Advisory, not a gate. Read-only.

sweep_id.description: List the comparisons on a sweep.

run_id.description: List the comparisons on a pre-prod run.

name: get_preprod_comparison
description: The candidate-vs-BASELINE verdict for one pre-prod run: the candidate's pass rate, the REGRESSION set (baseline passed, candidate failed), the new passes, and cost/latency/step deltas. The baseline is the run's own — a prior run or a prod window — and `baseline` overrides which. `regressionAnalysis` says how badly and WHERE: per failure mode, scorer category and scorer, the pass-rate delta with its 95% interval, `change` (a regression/improvement only when the interval excludes zero, else unchanged — small golden sets are noisy) and a severity (minor/moderate/severe); quote its `summary`. `noise` is the measured run-to-run noise band: when `withinNoise` is true the overall delta is indistinguishable from noise, so do not call it a regression or an improvement; when `status` is unmeasured say so and offer measure_preprod_noise (it re-runs the run unchanged and costs money). The noise band never changes `change` or the CI verdict. Two reporting rules: read `regressionCount`, not the length of the capped `regressions` evidence list; and a null passRate or null cost delta means NO DATA (nothing scored, nothing priced), never zero.

baseline.description: Override the run's stored baseline kind.

name: get_preprod_metrics
description: PER-METRIC score rollup for one pre-prod run — average and pass rate grouped by metric key. This is the CI-gate surface: it enforces 'faithfulness must stay ≥ 0.8' where the run's single aggregate pass rate cannot. `scored: 0` on a run that has captured nothing is an honest answer, not an error.

name: get_preprod_noise
description: How much two IDENTICAL runs of a pre-prod run's golden set differ: its run-to-run noise band. status 'measured' (from k-repeats, sweep arms or an earlier re-run) gives flipRate and runIds; 'unmeasured' means only one such run exists, so no band is claimed — canMeasure says whether Neens can re-run it, and estimate what that costs (totalUsd null = unpriced). Spends nothing.

name: get_preprod_run_items
description: The run's FROZEN prompt list: one row per golden item with its `itemId`, input and expected output. The itemId is the stable id a harness stamps as `neens.dataset_item_id`, and the `item_id` get_preprod_trajectory diffs on. A multi-turn item carries `conversation`: its user turns in order with each turn's replay status, reply, error and (with per-turn scoring) verdict — use it to say WHICH turn of a conversation went wrong.

name: get_preprod_trajectory
description: Diff HOW the agent behaved on ONE golden prompt between a candidate and a baseline pre-prod run: each run's captured trajectory reduced to an ordered tool-call/LLM step list, LCS-aligned, with added/removed/changed steps. Use after get_preprod_comparison to explain WHY an item regressed. A null sessionId means that run captured nothing for the prompt, so its side of the diff is empty — which is not the same as 'no change'.

name: get_prompt_fix_simulation
description: Poll a prompt fix simulation by id (from simulate_prompt_fix): status (queued|running|completed|failed), the overall and per-judge before/after scores, whether the replay diverged, and the replayed answer. A failed simulation carries its reason in `error`.

name: get_prompt_optimization
description: Poll a prompt-optimization run by id: status (queued|running|completed|failed|cancelled), the baseline vs best HELD-OUT score and the improvement, rollouts and iterations spent, the candidate lineage with Pareto/winner flags, the verdict, the markdown proof report, and the emitted remediation id when the winner cleared the bar. A run that never beat baseline completes with emit=false — a legitimate result, not an error.

name: get_remediation
description: Fetch one remediation by id with its simulations and what-changed correlation. The reply carries the grounded-flow evidence: failureLocus (where the failure lives), actionability (`actionable` = agent-fixable, `advisory` = a downstream/upstream service issue owned by owningComponent, not a prompt fix), groundingStatus (needs_grounding items are not yet concrete/confident), rootCauseSignature (the dedup key), fixability, and a likelyCause synthesized from the dominant error signature. `status` is the fix's lifecycle (proposed→accepted→applied→verified); `workState` is only the team's triage lane — never report a `done` workState as a shipped fix. Read groundingCaveats before acting: `evidence_disagreement` means the diagnosis and the agent's own evidence disagree, so the recommendation's mitigation claim is unverified. Use to review a fix's evidence before accepting/applying it — and note that moving it to applied/verified requires a bound proof: proofBound / proofReason / proofHint carry the server's own answer (a simulation alone is not a bound proof; see update_remediation). fixabilityVerdict says whether a patch can fix the failure: `patchable` (a fix run verified a patch), `capability_limited` (a model sweep on the failure's golden set shows the current model below the bar while a stronger model clears it — recommend a model change via that sweep, do not start another fix run; Neens never switches models itself) or `unknown` (follow recommendation.action, e.g. run_model_sweep on recommendation.datasetId).

name: get_trace
description: Fetch one trace (session) by id: agent, status, timing, error, a summary of its spans, the conversation (what the user asked and what the agent finally answered, as ordered role/content turns), and each tool call's arguments and result. Long content is truncated with a trailing '…' and `complete` is false when anything was cut. Use to read the evidence before diagnosing a failure, annotating the trace, or writing a judge example from it.

name: get_verification_run
description: Poll a verification (pre-prod) run by id for its proven verdict: status, whether it passed the gate, the failure reasons, regressions, pass rate, score aggregate, the gate and judges it was judged by, and — when items failed to run — captured/scored/errored counts, the top itemErrors and a failureClass (endpoint, judges or scoring). An item error 'scoring never completed after N attempts' means the run settled without it. `coverage` says whether the pass rate covers enough of the items: a run where more than max_error_rate (default 10%) of items errored or never ran fails, with a reason naming the count. Use to check a run started by run_verification that hadn't finished yet.

name: lint_prompt
description: Lint an agent system prompt or a SKILL.md file with Neens's deterministic rules (no LLM): steps numbered with one objective each, commands followed by a check of their result, error-recovery guidance present, no 'try again' as recovery, no contradictory instructions, a token budget (estimated as characters / 4, default 5,000), and for skills the frontmatter name and a specific description plus the 500-line body guidance. Pass exactly one of: prompt_id (a saved prompt; version or label picks one, newest by default), trace_id (the system prompts that trace actually ran under), or text (pasted prompt or SKILL.md). Each finding has ruleId, severity (error|warning|info), line, the quoted text it fired on, a plain-language message and a concrete suggestion. Read-only: to turn a finding into a remediation, use the Create fix button on the prompt's page.

version.description: With prompt_id: the version to lint (default newest).

label.description: With prompt_id: a deploy label such as production.

text.description: Prompt or SKILL.md text to lint.

kind.description: For text: auto (default) detects SKILL.md frontmatter.

name: list_ablation_runs
description: This agent's ablation runs, newest first, with status and sections.

name: list_agent_endpoints
description: List the agent endpoints this project can evaluate against: id, name, base URL, request shape (openai_chat | input_json), invoke path, model and auth mode. The id is the agent_connection_id that create_preprod_run (push mode), start_model_sweep arms and run_verification take. Credentials are never returned; hasCredential says whether a token is on file.

q.description: Match on name, URL or model.

name: list_agent_versions
description: List this agent's versions — the labels its traces carry — with what is known about each: group (serving = production traffic in the window, tested = no traffic in the window but measured by a model sweep or seen in production before, test = only on pre-prod runs and their replays, unversioned = traces with no label), isLive, tracesInWindow, lastSeenAt, sweepCount and the latest sweep id. The window never removes a version from the list; it only sets each version's group and traffic count. Pass a versionLabel as version to get_cost_quality_brief, or '__unversioned__' for the unlabelled traces.

window.description: Trailing window in days, e.g. '7d' (default) or '30d'.

name: list_ambient_runs
description: Scout's run log for this agent (Scout is the Neens agent behind the ambient tools), newest first: each investigation it ran on its own after an event (an alert, new insights, a finished clustering run, a fix's efficacy verdict, a judge drifting from reviewers, a new agent version). Each run has id, triggerKind, status (queued, running, waiting = paused until a long-running job ends, completed, failed, cancelled, skipped_no_connection = no LLM connection is configured, budget_refused = the agent's budget could not cover it, stopped = a guardrail ended it — reason wait_expired when the job it waited on outlived its 24 h / 72 h limit), reason, waitingOn (the job a waiting run waits for, with when the wait expires) and, when completed, the finding's title (agent-written, in the reader's language when it could be translated). Filter with status; include_memory adds what the agent remembers from earlier runs (its notes: conclusion, ids, date).

include_memory.description: Also return the agent's memory notes.

name: list_assignable_users
description: List the people a fix (remediation) can be assigned to: members of the company who can access its agent, as {id, name, role}. `name` is the display name, or for someone without one the part of their email before the @ (never a full address). Pass the returned `id` as update_remediation's assignee_id — e.g. for 'assign the top fix to Kenji', call this with q='Kenji', then update_remediation. Anyone not listed would be refused. Needs a signed-in person's credential (an agent API key cannot list people).

remediation_id.description: The fix's id (from list_remediations, get_remediation or get_action_inbox's remediationId).

q.description: Only people whose name contains this text (case-insensitive).

name: list_clusters
description: List the ACTIVE failure clusters from the latest clustering run — id, label, description, session count and L1 bucket. The id is what list_traces takes as `cluster_id` to get that cluster's exact traces. Use this rather than matching a cluster's name. (list_failure_modes is the richer hero view of the same run, with readiness and root-cause hypotheses.)

name: list_code_environments
description: List the custom code environments this project can use: extra Python packages, beyond a runtime's own, that code (custom_python) judges can import. Each has a status; only status ready (usable: true) can be passed as environment_id to test_code_judge, create_judge or create_judge_version.

name: list_code_runtimes
description: List the Python runtimes code (custom_python) judges run on, with the exact packages each can import, the time/memory limits, and whether code execution is enabled on this deployment.

name: list_components
description: List the components this agent invoked in a window — skills, MCP servers, sub-agents and tools — with invocations, sessions reached, errorRate, latency p50/p95 (ms), versions seen, agentInvokedShare (the agent chose it vs a person typed its command; null when the trace did not record who), costUsd of the model calls made inside it (null = unpriced, never $0) and the components most often used with it. Rates are null over fewer than minInvocations invocations (thin). Cost and co-use are measured over the newest sessions (sampleComplete says whether that was every one). Use get_component for one component's recent invocations.

name: list_dataset_versions
description: List a dataset's immutable VERSIONS (snapshots), newest first, and name which one is golden. A pre-prod run and a model sweep both replay a frozen version, and create_preprod_run resolves the GOLDEN one when you give it no version — so check here first if a run refuses with 'dataset has no golden version'.

name: list_datasets
description: List the project's datasets: id, name, item count, source kind, tags and the cluster a from-cluster dataset was built from. Use to find an existing dataset before creating one, or to get the id the version/export/pre-prod tools take.

name: list_enrichments
description: List the enrichments in this project — per-trace tags/values computed by an LLM prompt, an external API or code — with each one's id, mode, status (draft / enabled), trigger (manual / on_ingest), output fields, latest run and, for a code (custom_python) enrichment, its current code. Use it to find an enrichment id for test_code_enrichment, create_enrichment_version or deploy_enrichment.

name: list_eval_gates
description: List the project's eval gates — the failure modes CI replays on every build — with ONE reconciled status each (`health`): `state` is the newest CI check (passed | failed | no_data | pending | error | never_in_ci); `warnings` may hold `stale` (an enforced gate CI has not checked for `staleAfterDays`) and `judge_misses_failure` (the evidence check passes at or above the threshold, so the judge passes the failure itself and a CI pass proves nothing) and `saturated` (CI passed 100% in each of the last `saturateAfterRuns` runs, so the gate no longer tells good builds from bad; advisory only, suggest adding harder real failing cases), worded in `warningMessages`. `evidenceCatchRate` (1 − evidencePassRate; null = not checked yet) is the share of the gate's own past failures the judge catches — higher is better, like the CI pass rate. Also returns the newest CI build's single `summaryVerdict`. Filter by status (active | paused) or needs_attention.

needs_attention.description: Only gates whose status is a warning or a failure.

name: list_failure_modes
description: Summarize the latest failure-clustering run: readiness, the failure modes ranked by impact (label, description, session counts, NEW flags, root-cause hypotheses, fix-loop stage, who can fix it — owner agent | external | unclassified — traces in the window vs the previous window, and each mode's ONE primaryAction), plus the page's `briefing`: plain-language sentences, the owner split, chips and up to 3 nextActions. An `external` mode (stage `downstream`) is escalated to the service that owns it, never fixed in the agent. Use to understand what's failing before generating a remediation or a judge.

range.description: Time window, compared with the previous window of the same length (default 7d; `all` has no previous window).

name: list_judge_disagreements
description: The traces where a judge and the human gold label DISAGREE, with both verdicts, the judge's score and reason, and the human's critique. type 'false_positive' is a false alarm (judge failed it, human passed it); 'false_negative' is a miss (judge passed a real failure). Computed live from the current labels and scores. Use to decide what to change in the judge before create_judge_version.

judge_id.description: Judge id from list_judges, or its name (required).

type.description: Only false alarms, or only misses.

name: list_judges
description: List the project's judges (scorers) with their versions and DEPLOYMENTS. Each deployment carries the `id` that run_eval and create_preprod_run need, plus its trigger, status and last run — so picking a judge to score with takes one call. Quality travels too: each deployment's lastResult (pass rate of its latest finished run) and each judge's agreement with human labels (Cohen's kappa from its newest measurement within the last agreement.windowDays days; low=true below the trust floor; null when not measured in that window). Use before run_eval, or to find an existing judge instead of creating a duplicate. (list_scores is different: it reports how each METRIC is trending.)

name: list_model_sweeps
description: List this project's model sweeps, newest first: id, name, status, version label, created time and each sweep's arms (label, model, status). Filter with `q` (matches the sweep name or version label) or `status`. Use it to recover a sweep id — e.g. when a start_model_sweep reply was lost to a timeout — BEFORE launching again: a sweep that already exists must not be relaunched. Then read it with get_model_sweep / get_model_sweep_comparison.

q.description: Case-insensitive match on the sweep name or version label.

name: list_open_remediations
description: List the OPEN backlog of AGENT-FIXABLE remediations, ranked by priority. By default this is only what a coding agent can actually implement and prove: status proposed/accepted, grounded (a concrete, confident fix), and actionable (agent_reasoning / tool_contract / quality). It EXCLUDES verified/closed + archived items (include_resolved=true), advisory items — downstream/upstream service failures that name a service owner, not a prompt fix (include_advisories=true), and needs_grounding items held back until concrete+confident (include_ungrounded=true). Each row carries failureLocus, actionability, owningComponent (for advisories), its lifecycle status, any PR/commit reported, and the last verification run id. Use this to find the next fix to implement + prove.

include_advisories.description: Also include advisory (infra/downstream/upstream) items that name a service owner rather than an agent-fixable change. Default false.

include_ungrounded.description: Also include needs_grounding items held out of the backlog until they are concrete and confident. Default false.

name: list_papercuts
description: List the papercuts this agent filed about itself (neens.papercut span events: what it tried, expected, what happened, and its suggested fix), grouped — reports about the same component whose 'happened' text matches once ids, numbers, quoted values, paths and URLs are masked are one group. These are the AGENT'S OWN CLAIMS (source agent_reported), never a verdict: confirm against the traces before acting. Each group has groupKey, reports, sessions, the component, the latest report, linked failure modes and the remediation it was promoted to (null if none). Filter by component_kind + component_name.

name: list_preprod_runs
description: List the project's pre-prod eval runs, newest first: status, version label, dataset + FROZEN dataset version id, gate, progress and regression count. The datasetVersionId is what tells you which runs are comparable — compare_preprod_runs requires runs that share one. Filter by status or dataset_id.

status.description: awaiting_traces | running | completed | completed_with_regressions | failed | cancelled.

name: list_remediations
description: List suggested fixes (remediations) ranked by priority, with a stats rollup. Filter by status, workState, clusterId, failureModeId, or type. Each row carries failureLocus (where the failure lives) and actionability: `actionable` items are agent-fixable in-repo, `advisory` items are downstream/upstream service failures that name an owningComponent instead of a prompt fix, and non_actionable covers working-as-intended controls; groundingStatus flags items held as needs_grounding until concrete+confident. Use to see the full backlog before transitioning a remediation's lifecycle. (For only the agent-fixable open backlog, use list_open_remediations.)

status.description: proposed | accepted | applied | verified | closed | regressed.

name: list_score_rows
description: List INDIVIDUAL score rows — one per scored trace/session — with the judge's score, label and reason, filterable by metric_key, pass/fail `status`, score range, target, source or a specific eval `run_id`. This is the per-row read; list_scores is the aggregate rollup. Use to find WHICH traces a judge failed. `evidence` holds the verbatim trace quotes the verdict cited — quote them when explaining a verdict. `run_id` reads that run's own snapshot and cannot be combined with metric_key, source or range — that branch applies none of them, so it is refused rather than answered with unfiltered rows.

status.description: Compared against each row's own threshold.

run_id.description: Restrict to one eval run's own snapshot. Mutually exclusive with metric_key / source / range.

lifecycle.description: Default finalized — experimental judges are hidden.

sort.description: Default latest. 'lowest' surfaces the worst first.

name: list_scores
description: List the score types / scorers active in the project and how each is trending: metric key, label, source, target type, average, scored count, pass rate, and period-over-period delta. Use to see eval coverage and quality trends.

name: list_standing_instructions
description: Your own standing instructions for Scout on this agent: each one's id, name, text, schedule (cron, time zone, next run) or condition (the event it waits for), status (active, paused, ended + why), last result and waitingOn (level = Scout is not set to investigate on this agent, paused, quarantined). Pass instruction_id to read one with its latest results (Scout's findings). Only the person who set an instruction can see it.

instruction_id.description: Read this one, with its latest results.

name: list_traces
description: List/search agent traces (sessions) in the current project. Filter by status, agent, FAILURE CLUSTER (`cluster_id` — the exact membership set, from list_clusters / list_failure_modes), score metric/label/status, issue mode, failure set, model, tool name, tags, source, agent version, free text, time bounds, conversation, and duration/token ranges. Returns the total match count and up to `limit` summary rows. Use to find traces to inspect, annotate, or add to a dataset.

cluster_id.description: Failure-cluster id (from list_clusters / list_failure_modes) — the exact membership set, never a name match. Prefer this over issue_mode.

score_status.description: pass | fail — use together with score_metric.

score_label.description: Exact score LABEL, e.g. a classifier's class name.

failure_set.description: Restrict to the clustering failure set.

model.description: Model names; repeatable (OR within the filter).

tool_name.description: Tool names the trace called; repeatable (OR).

version.description: Agent version (the neens.version_label span attribute), exact match; '__unversioned__' selects traces with none.

started_after.description: ISO 8601 lower bound on trace start time.

started_before.description: ISO 8601 upper bound on trace start time.

name: measure_preprod_noise
description: Measure the noise band: re-run a completed PUSH pre-prod run UNCHANGED (same frozen items, endpoint, model, judges, prompt) so its delta can be read against real run-to-run spread. Spends money: refused when the estimate exceeds budget_usd or the platform ceiling; dry_run=true returns only the estimate. A run driven by your own harness cannot be re-run by Neens; run your harness again instead and the band is derived automatically.

budget_usd.description: Refuse when the estimate exceeds this.

name: promote_papercut
description: Promote one papercut group (groupKey from list_papercuts) to a remediation in the backlog: titled from the report, typed from its component (tool / MCP server → a tool schema change, skill / sub-agent → a prompt change), linked to the failure mode its traces fell into, marked needs grounding because it rests on the agent's own report. Idempotent: a group already promoted returns the existing remediation (created false).

name: propose_ablation_fix
description: Turn a 'removing_it_helps' section into a proposed prompt_change fix (before: the full prompt, after: without the section). It is verified and merged like any fix; nothing changes in the agent until a person merges it.

arm_id.description: The section's arm id from get_ablation_run (required).

name: rate_next_action
description: Rate one next action useful or not_useful (clear removes your rating), with an optional short note saying why. Use it after acting on, or deciding to skip, an action from get_next_actions. Only your own rating changes. A rating from an agent or an API key is stored as an agent rating: people see it, but it never changes how actions rank (counted is false).

rating.description: useful, not_useful, or clear to remove your rating.

name: record_fix_merge
description: Tell Neens a fix PR was MERGED so it can start a post-merge efficacy close-out: Neens stamps a deploy event + a close-out watch and, after the post-deploy window, measures the fixed failure mode's real production volume before vs after and auto-verifies (or flags a regression of) the remediation. remediation_id is required; pr_url/commit_sha default from the remediation, merged_at defaults to now. Optionally send the merged `diff` / `changed_files` so the change is readable in Neens.

pr_url.description: The merged PR url (else the remediation's).

diff.description: The fix's unified diff (`git diff` output), shown in Neens so people without access to the repository can read the change. Redacted and capped at 200 KB; over the cap the file list is kept and the diff is marked truncated.

changed_files.description: The changed files with line counts (derived from `diff` when omitted).

name: regenerate_remediation
description: Regenerate a remediation with the current engine, archiving the prior one as a superseded predecessor; returns the fresh remediation. Use after the detection/remediation engine has changed, or new failing traces have arrived, to re-run the current grounded engine for the same failure source (cluster or failure mode). The old proposal is preserved (archived + superseded, restorable) — nothing is deleted, and its PR/verification state is kept. The reply carries regeneratedFromId (the archived predecessor).

name: register_agent_endpoint
description: Register the HTTP endpoint of an agent so Neens can call it with test cases (push runs, model sweeps, verification). Re-registering the same name and URL updates it. request_shape 'openai_chat' posts a chat-completions body (with `model`); 'input_json' posts {input} and reads {output}. The URL must be reachable from Neens — private, loopback and link-local addresses are refused unless the deployment allows them. auth_token is stored encrypted and never returned. Call list_agent_endpoints first to reuse an existing endpoint.

base_url.description: http(s) base URL of the agent (required). May carry a query string, which is kept at the end of every call; a #fragment is refused.

invoke_path.description: Path joined onto base_url's PATH, e.g. /invoke (default /chat/completions for openai_chat, none for input_json). https://h/agent?v=2 + /invoke calls https://h/agent/invoke?v=2. A query key may be set in base_url or invoke_path, not both.

model.description: Model id sent in an openai_chat body.

output_jsonpath.description: Where to read the answer in a custom reply, e.g. data.answer.

accepts_system_prompt.description: True when the agent uses a system prompt Neens sends (the leading system message, or input_json's system_prompt field). Ablation runs need it.

name: release_ambient_quarantine
description: Release a target Scout stopped investigating after repeated failed runs (admin). Its next event starts a run again and its failure count restarts. Take the id from get_ambient_settings. There is no undo: if it keeps failing it is held again.

name: report_fix_status
description: Report a fix's progress back to Neens: set the remediation's lifecycle `status` (proposed|accepted|applied|verified|closed|regressed) and/or `work_state` (todo|in_progress|done|archived), and record the `pr_url` + `commit_sha` where the fix landed. Also send the fix's `diff` (and/or `changed_files`) so people who cannot open the PR (a private repository) can read the change in Neens. remediation_id + at least one other field required. Use after opening a PR or applying a fix so the loop is auditable.

pr_url.description: The PR the fix was opened in (http/https).

commit_sha.description: The commit the fix landed on.

diff.description: The fix's unified diff (`git diff` output), shown in Neens so people without access to the repository can read the change. Redacted and capped at 200 KB; over the cap the file list is kept and the diff is marked truncated.

changed_files.description: The changed files with line counts (derived from `diff` when omitted).

name: run_eval
description: Start an evaluation run for a deployed judge. Pass deployment_id (list_judges → deployments[].id, or deploy_judge's reply) OR just judge_id, in which case that judge's single enabled deployment is used — if it has none, or more than one, the tool says so and names the candidates. Never guess a deployment id. Scores the deployment's targeted traces and writes scores. By default the DEPLOYMENT's sampling filter decides how many traces a run covers; pass sample_size to cap THIS run at that many of the deployment's eligible traces (most-recent first) without editing the deployment — e.g. sample_size=1000 to score 1000 traces. Pass target_ids (trace ids) or dataset_id to score EXACTLY those traces instead — e.g. the traces the user already labeled, to check the judge against them; every id must be a trace in this project, and sample_size still caps the set. A run scores at most the per-run maximum (2,000 traces by default): a larger sample_size, or more target_ids than that, is refused — split the work into several runs. If sample_size is omitted and the deployment would score more, the run scores an evenly spaced sample of the maximum and says sampleCapped=true. Returns the run id, status, resolvedDeploymentId, total (the number actually queued, which is smaller than sample_size when fewer traces are eligible), eligibleCount (how many traces it was drawn from), sampleCapped and maxSampleSize.

deployment_id.description: Judge deployment id. Omit it and pass judge_id to use the judge's enabled deployment.

judge_id.description: Judge id — resolves that judge's enabled deployment when deployment_id is omitted.

sample_size.description: Cap THIS run at this many of the deployment's eligible traces (most-recent first), leaving the deployment's sampling filter unchanged. At most the per-run maximum (2,000 by default). Omit to let the deployment decide the count, up to that maximum.

target_ids.description: Score EXACTLY these trace ids instead of the deployment's eligible traces. Not with dataset_id.

dataset_id.description: Score the traces in this dataset (id or name). Not with target_ids.

name: run_verification
description: PROVE a fix works: trigger a REAL pre-prod PUSH evaluation that calls the given candidate endpoint (endpoint_url — a preview deployment/branch, plus invoke_path when the agent listens on a sub-path — or an existing agent_connection_id) with the remediation's golden dataset, scores every response, and gates it. version_label (the branch/commit/preview id) is required. Pass remediation_id to derive the golden dataset, gate thresholds and scoring judge from its proof gate and stamp the result back onto the fix; judge_deployment_ids picks the judges and baseline_run_id compares against a prior run on the same items. The reply echoes the effective gate, judges and baseline plus `warnings` when the verdict would be weak. Polls up to wait_seconds and returns pass/fail, reasons, pass rate, regressions and, when items failed to run, itemErrors + failureClass (endpoint = your endpoint never answered, judges = nothing was scored, scoring = scoring never completed — none is a verdict on the fix); if still running, poll get_verification_run with the runId.

remediation_id.description: Ties the run to a fix + derives its golden dataset.

endpoint_url.description: Preview deployment URL to PUSH-eval. A path in the URL is kept (e.g. https://preview.example.com/eval/invoke), and so is a query string: invoke_path is joined onto the URL's PATH, and the query stays at the end. A #fragment is refused (servers never receive it).

invoke_path.description: Path joined onto endpoint_url's path, e.g. /eval/invoke (default: the URL itself for input_json, /chat/completions for openai_chat). https://h/p?v=2 + /chat/completions calls https://h/p/chat/completions?v=2. A query key may be set in endpoint_url or invoke_path, not both.

agent_connection_id.description: OR an existing agent endpoint connection (id, or its unique name).

auth_token.description: Optional bearer token for endpoint_url (stored encrypted).

dataset_id.description: Explicit golden dataset (else derived from remediation).

dataset_version_id.description: A specific frozen dataset version (default: the golden version).

min_pass_rate.description: Gate: minimum pass rate (0–1). Default: the remediation's proof gate, else the deployment default.

max_regressions.description: Gate: max allowed regressions. Default: the remediation's proof gate (0).

max_error_rate.description: Gate: the share of items (0–1) allowed to error or not run before the run fails on coverage. Default 0.1.

judge_deployment_ids.description: Judge deployments that score the run (from list_judges). Default: the proof gate's judge, else the project default.

baseline_kind.description: What regressions are measured against. Default prod_window (7d of production scores).

baseline_run_id.description: A prior run on the same dataset (e.g. the current version verified under version_label 'main') to compare against item by item.

wait_seconds.description: How long to poll for a verdict (default 90, max 300).

name: set_expected_tool_calls
description: Record the CORRECT trajectory on one dataset item: the tools the agent should call, in what order, with what arguments.
