This is the ground truth the deterministic Tool Selection / Tool Sequence / Tool Arguments scorers grade pre-prod runs and fix verification against. add_to_dataset prefills a DRAFT from the trace's actual calls (expectedToolCallsReviewed: false, never graded) — read it with get_dataset_items, correct it, and save it here, which marks it reviewed. `expected_tool_calls` is a list of {name, args, match} where match is exact|subset|any (default exact); `order` is strict|relaxed|any (default relaxed: expected calls in order, extra calls allowed); an empty list means 'no tools should be called'. clear: true removes them (the scorers then skip the item); prefill_from_trace: true re-copies the draft from the item's trace. Edits the live item; snapshot a new golden version for runs to see it.

order.description: How strictly the order is checked (default relaxed).

prefill_from_trace.description: Replace with a draft copied from the trace.

clear.description: Remove the item's expected tool calls.

name: set_scoring_budget
description: Set this project's daily cap on automatic scoring: how many traces per UTC day each continuous (on-ingest) scorer may send to its judge. Admins only — a project API key can read the cap (list_judges → deployments[].dailyCap) but gets an error here. 0 pauses automatic scoring; clear=true removes the project value so the company default (or the platform default of 500) applies. Scorers with their own per-scorer cap keep it. A value above the company's daily scoring ceiling (the response's `ceiling`; null = unlimited) is rejected.

max_scored_per_day.description: Traces per scorer per UTC day (0 = paused).

clear.description: true clears the project value (inherit the company/platform default) instead of setting one.

name: simulate_prompt_fix
description: Cheap PRE-CHECK for a system-prompt fix: replay ONE real failing trace (session_id) with an edited system prompt and re-score the new answer with the judges that graded the original. Tool calls are answered from the results recorded in the trace — no live traffic, nothing deployed, no production score overwritten. Returns overall + per-judge scoreBefore/scoreAfter and pass counts. diverged=true (the edited prompt called a tool the trace never recorded) or exhausted=true pins every after-score to its before-score — inconclusive, not a regression. Makes real, billable model calls on the agent's LLM connection and is rate-limited. One trace is NOT proof: prove the fix with run_verification on the golden set. If the reply has pending=true, poll get_prompt_fix_simulation.

session_id.description: Id of the failing trace to replay (required).

judge_ids.description: Judges to score with (default: the LLM judges that scored this trace). Ids not visible to this agent are refused, never silently swapped.

connection_id.description: LLM connection to replay with (default: the agent's default connection).

name: start_ablation_run
description: Does each part of the system prompt earn its tokens? Replays one frozen golden set through the agent's endpoint with the full prompt (full_repeats times, default 2, which also measures the noise band) and once per named section with that ONE section removed, then gives each section a verdict: earns_its_place, no_measurable_effect or removing_it_helps, with the quality delta (95% interval), cost delta and latency delta. Give the prompt as prompt_id (prompt management) or system_prompt (text). Sections are Markdown headings or <tag> blocks: call with dry_run=true first to list their keys and the cost estimate. The endpoint must accept a system prompt from Neens (register_agent_endpoint accepts_system_prompt). Only prompt sections can be ablated, not tools (your agent owns its tools). Spends money; refused above budget_usd. Never changes the live prompt. Poll get_ablation_run.

dataset_version_id.description: A frozen version instead of the golden.

sections.description: Section keys to remove, one arm each.

budget_usd.description: Refuse when the estimate exceeds this.

dry_run.description: List sections and estimate only; start nothing.

name: start_fix_run
description: Launch a Neens-ORCHESTRATED, eval-verified fix run for an accepted remediation: Neens proposes a patch from the fix bundle, applies it on a branch, VERIFIES it with pass^k pre-prod runs against the remediation's failure-derived evals + the regression set, and ONLY if green opens a PR (a human still merges). Requires remediation_id (with a resolvable proof-gate dataset). Returns the queued/terminal fix-run — poll it with get_fix_run. Optional: driver, vcs_installation_id, endpoint_url, version_label, pass_k, max_attempts.

vcs_installation_id.description: VCS installation to open the PR against.

endpoint_url.description: Preview deploy URL to PUSH-verify against.

agent_connection_id.description: OR an existing agent_http connection id.

name: start_model_sweep
description: Launch a MULTI-MODEL SWEEP: replay ONE frozen golden dataset version against N candidate model arms, k times each, and report pass^k PER ARM — the evidence for 'which model should we ship'. Every arm runs under IDENTICAL conditions (same frozen items, same judges, same k, same gate); only the model differs. Requires name, version_label, and arms. Two kinds of arm, never mixed in one sweep: PUSH arms {label, agent_connection_id} name a registered agent_http endpoint per model that Neens calls; RUNNER arms {label, model, runner_mode: 'runner'} need no endpoint — Neens NEVER calls in, the CALLER drives them: run `neens sweep run --sweep-id <id> -- <your agent command>`, which runs the agent once per arm × repetition × item with NEENS_EVAL_MODEL set to the arm's model and sends the traces. Use runner arms for a local or CI agent with no public URL. A runner sweep starts awaiting_traces and its arms list the child run ids. Give dataset_id (its golden version is used), dataset_version_id, or scenario_suite_id. Cost is bounded: the sweep is refused if it exceeds budget_usd or the deployment's arm/k/run ceilings. Returns the queued sweep — poll it with get_model_sweep. sampleSize says what the golden set can prove: perfectScoreProves (20 items prove at most ~84%) and itemsForBar (35 for a 90% bar); code too_few means even a perfect score cannot prove the bar. Preview the cost first with POST /model-sweeps/preview if you want an estimate before spending. If this call times out, do NOT relaunch: find the sweep with list_model_sweeps (q = its name) first.

version_label.description: Candidate version label — the branch/commit/deploy every arm is evaluated at (required).

arms.description: One entry per model under comparison (required). All push or all runner. Two arms on the SAME connection (push) or the SAME model (runner) is not a comparison and is rejected.

label.description: Display name for the arm, e.g. 'sonnet'.

agent_connection_id.description: PUSH arm: id of a registered agent_http connection whose endpoint runs that model.

model.description: RUNNER arm: the model id your agent is told to run (NEENS_EVAL_MODEL), e.g. 'claude-haiku-4-5'.

runner_mode.description: 'push' (default): Neens calls agent_connection_id. 'runner': the caller drives the arm with `neens sweep run`; requires model.

dataset_id.description: Golden dataset to replay (its frozen golden version is snapshotted).

scenario_suite_id.description: Or a ready synthetic scenario suite, whose frozen version is used.

pass_k.description: Repeat runs per arm (default per config, clamped to the deployment cap). k>1 is what defeats a flaky green.

judge_deployment_ids.description: Graders (default: the project's deployed judges). Pinned once, reused by every arm.

budget_usd.description: Refuse to launch if the pre-flight estimate exceeds this.

gate.description: The quality bar every arm is judged against: min_pass_rate (0-1), max_regressions and max_error_rate (0-1, default 0.1: a run with more errored items is not green). Omit for the default; a re-run of an earlier sweep carries its gate.

name: start_pairwise_comparison
description: Run a BLIND PAIRWISE comparison: a judge of type 'pairwise' (create one with create_judge, type='pairwise') reads each shared golden input with the two answers labelled A and B — never which model or version wrote them — and says which is better, or tie. Which side is A is randomized per item from a recorded seed, and by default every item is judged in BOTH orders; a pair whose verdict flips with the order counts as a tie. Give sweep_id (two arms of a model sweep; default the first two arms) OR run_id (a settled pre-prod run against its baseline, or baseline_run_id). SPENDS LLM BUDGET on the tenant's connection: 2 judge calls per item with both orders. Refused when the estimate exceeds budget_usd (default: the deployment cap) — an unpriced judge model has an unknown cost (null), never $0. ADVISORY: it never changes a gate's pass/fail. Poll with get_pairwise_comparison.

sweep_id.description: Compare two arms of this sweep.

run_id.description: Compare this settled pre-prod run to its baseline.

both_orders.description: Judge each pair in both orders (default true). false halves the cost and loses the position-bias control.

budget_usd.description: Refuse to launch above this estimate.

name: start_preprod_run
description: Start a created pre-prod run. Routes itself: a 'push' run is executed by Neens against its agent endpoint, a 'runner' run is moved to `running` to await your harness's traces — the tool reads the run's own runner_mode, so you do not have to pick. Refuses a run that is already terminal. Under an inline queue the returned run may already be finished; otherwise poll it with list_preprod_runs or read the verdict with get_preprod_comparison.

mode.description: Override the run's own runner_mode (rarely needed).

name: start_prompt_optimization
description: Launch an OFFLINE, GEPA-style prompt-optimization run for a confirmed failure mode: Neens replays that mode's HISTORICAL traces under candidate system prompts (tool results served from each recorded trace — no live traffic), grades every rollout with the project's judges, reflects on the graded trajectories, and proves the winner on a held-out split. A winner that clears the bar is emitted as a normal prompt_change remediation you can then fix-run (start_fix_run) — it is a PROPOSAL, never a deploy. Requires failure_mode_id (preferred), cluster_id, or session_ids. Returns the queued/terminal run — poll it with get_prompt_optimization.

failure_mode_id.description: Seed failure mode (preferred — its eval gate becomes the emitted fix's proof gate).

objective.description: Free-text steer for the reflection step.

max_rollouts.description: Rollout budget (clamped to the deployment cap).

name: test_code_enrichment
description: Test-run code (custom_python) enrichment code on up to 3 of this project's traces in the sandbox WITHOUT saving anything. Pass code + output_fields, or enrichment_id to test a saved code enrichment's current code (any code fields you pass override it). Each result carries the values the code returned per field, printed stdout and, on failure, the error class + line. A trace id that is not in this project is reported in notInProject and never read. The code is a top-level `def enrich(target)` or `def enrich(target, ctx)`; `target` is a dict of the required_data keys (input, output, messages, context, metadata). It returns a dict keyed by the output field keys, each value of that field's type (boolean → true/false, number, string, enum → one of its values, array → a list of scalars); a key that is not a declared field or a value of the wrong type fails the trace, and a field left out is simply not set. `ctx.skip("reason")` skips a trace. It runs in the same isolated sandbox as code judges: NO network, nothing installable, no secrets, nothing persists between traces. Needs a plan with code enrichments (Gold).

enrichment_id.description: A saved code enrichment to test.

output_fields.description: The values the code returns, e.g. [{"key": "quotes_refund", "type": "boolean"}, {"key": "refund_amount", "type": "number"}]. type is boolean | number | string | enum (with values) | array.

trace_ids.description: Up to 3 trace ids (list_traces); omit for recent ones.

runtime.description: custom_python: runtime id to pin (default: the current one).

requirements.description: custom_python: requirements.txt lines the runtime must already meet (nothing is installed), e.g. "numpy>=2".

capabilities.description: custom_python: {"llm": true} to allow ctx.llm calls through the agent's LLM connection. Off by default.

environment_id.description: Optional: a code environment id (list_code_environments) whose extra packages the code imports.

required_data.description: Data to feed the code (input/output/messages/context/metadata; default input/output/messages/metadata).

name: test_code_judge
description: Test-run custom_python (code) judge code on up to 3 of this project's traces in the sandbox WITHOUT saving anything. Pass code (and output_spec, matching what the code returns), or judge_id to test a saved code judge's current code — any code fields you pass override it. trace_ids picks the traces (list_traces); omit them to use recent ones. Each result carries the verdict (score, pass, and label: the label the code returned on a binary/categorical output_spec), traceLabel (the trace's display name), printed stdout and, on failure, the error class + line. environment_id (list_code_environments) adds a custom environment's packages. A trace id that is not in this project is reported in notInProject and never read. The code is a top-level `def judge(target)` or `def judge(target, ctx)`; `target` is a dict of the required_data keys (output, input, messages, context, expected_output, metadata). It returns {"score": float} on the default 0–1 scale, or {"label": …} when output_spec is binary/categorical (the shape MUST match output_spec, or every trace fails with an invalid return value); `ctx.skip("reason")` skips a trace. The code runs in an isolated sandbox with NO network: external APIs, URLs and downloads all fail (requests imports but every call fails), nothing can be installed (only the runtime's packages), there are no secrets, and nothing persists between traces. The one way out is ctx.llm, with capabilities {"llm": true}. Needs a plan with code judges (Gold). type=composite tests a composite instead (unsaved: components + method; or a saved composite's judge_id): weighted_sum/expression combine each trace's EXISTING component scores and run nothing; method custom_python runs combine().

type.description: Default 'custom_python' (a code judge). 'composite' tests a composite judge.

code.description: Python source to test (omit to use judge_id's code).

judge_id.description: A saved custom_python (or composite) judge to test.

required_data.description: Data to feed the code (default input/output/messages/metadata).

output_spec.description: The judge's scale. Omit for 0–1. {"type": "binary", "pass_label": "pass", "fail_label": "fail"} for pass/fail; {"type": "categorical", "labels": [worst … best]}; {"type": "numeric_range", "min": 1, "max": 10}.

runtime.description: custom_python: runtime id to pin (default: the current one).

requirements.description: custom_python: requirements.txt lines the runtime must already meet (nothing is installed), e.g. "numpy>=2".

capabilities.description: custom_python: {"llm": true} to allow ctx.llm calls through the agent's LLM connection. Off by default.

environment_id.description: custom_python: id of a ready custom code environment (list_code_environments) whose extra packages the code imports. It must belong to this agent or be shared across the company; the judge is pinned to its exact build.

components.description: composite only (required): the judges to combine, by id (list_judges) or exact name, each with an optional weight (default: equal).

expression.description: composite method=expression: the formula over component metric keys, e.g. "min(cites_sources, polite_tone)".

threshold.description: composite: the 0–1 score at or above which it passes (default 0.7).

min_components.description: composite: skip a trace with fewer scored components than this (default 1).

missing_policy.description: composite: a trace missing a component score is skipped (default) or failed.

name: update_ambient_settings
description: Change this agent's Scout settings (admin). Send only what changes: level (off, suggest, investigate, act — act also lets it run the write tools in act_tools itself), act_tools (the full allowlist to store; [] allows none; only tools from actEligible: building a regression set, drafting a judge it never deploys, checking it against reviewers' verdicts, running an existing deployment), connection_id (the LLM connection investigations use; empty string = follow Scout chat's), budget_usd + budget_period (day, week, month), max_runs_per_day, max_concurrent_runs, paused (true stops every investigation at its next step). To undo, call it again with the previous values from get_ambient_settings.

connection_id.description: LLM connection id for investigations; empty string follows Scout chat's connection.

budget_usd.description: Most investigations may cost per period, in USD.

paused.description: true pauses every investigation (the kill switch).

act_tools.description: The whole write allowlist for the act level (replaces it).

name: update_remediation
description: Transition a remediation's lifecycle: `status` (proof lane: proposed|accepted|applied|verified|closed|regressed) and/or `work_state` (triage lane: todo|in_progress|done|archived) and/or `labels` and/or `assignee_id`. At least one required. Use to accept, progress, assign, or archive a fix. Moving an ACTIONABLE fix to `applied` or `verified` now requires a bound proof — a verification run (run_verification) or a bound eval gate — or an explicit force override with a reason; without one the transition is refused. Check get_remediation's proofBound first (a simulation alone does not count). Advisory / working_as_intended items have no agent eval and settle as `closed` with an acknowledgement note instead. `assignee_id` sets the fix's owner — a user id who can access this agent (anyone else is refused) — or "" to clear it. (Deleting remediations requires an admin over HTTP — not exposed here.)

assignee_id.description: Assign the fix to this user id (an `id` from list_assignable_users — anyone else is refused), or "" to clear the assignee.

name: update_standing_instruction
description: Change one of your standing instructions: paused (true stops it until resumed; false resumes it), text, name, cron + timezone, condition_kind (+ condition_target_id), slack, once. Send only what changes. To undo, call it again with the previous values from list_standing_instructions.

text.description: What Scout should do, in your words.

name.description: A short label (default: the first line).

condition_kind.description: Fire on this event instead of a schedule.

condition_target_id.description: Only events about this judge, fix, next action or agent version.

slack.description: Also DM results to you in Slack.
